papers.title: The Systematic Parameter Optimization of Displacement Reactions for Tailored ZnS Nanostructure Morphologies
papers.abstract: Precise regulation of zinc sulfide (ZnS) nanostructure morphology remains a significant objective in semiconductor materials research, as functional performance is highly sensitive to variations in particle size and geometry. This study presents a comprehensive evaluation of displacement reaction synthesis parameters to achieve controlled morphological engineering of ZnS nanostructures. The influence of precursor concentration, reaction temperature, pH, solvent characteristics, reaction time, and ionic strength on nucleation behavior and crystal growth dynamics was systematically examined. Through deliberate adjustment of these variables, diverse structural forms, including nanoparticles, nanorods, nanosheets, and hierarchical architectures, were consistently synthesized without relying on external templates or complex directing agents. The results demonstrate that supersaturation levels predominantly regulate nucleation rates, whereas temperature and pH significantly affect anisotropic growth and defect evolution. Additionally, solvent polarity and reaction duration contribute to surface energy stabilization and aggregation control, facilitating uniform crystallite size and structural homogeneity. Structural characterization verifies the formation of phase-pure, highly crystalline ZnS, while optical analysis reveals morphology-dependent shifts in band-gap energy attributable to quantum confinement and surface-state phenomena. Overall, the study delineates clear relationships between reaction conditions and resulting nanostructure morphology, providing a rational framework for scalable displacement-based synthesis of ZnS tailored for optoelectronic, photocatalytic, and sensing technologies.
